newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: TWO SHOT DEAD, TWO INJURED IN ROBBERY
No trace has been found of a gunman who shot two people dead and injured a woman and a man during a bungled jewellery robbery in central Melbourne today.
The shootings were on the eighth floor of the Century Building in Swanston Street, at Pin Gems.
Police have recovered a small calibre gun at the scene, and despite reports the gunman might still be in the building, nobody has been apprehended.
The dead and injured were all staff at Pin Gems, a wholesale gem dealer.
A wounded man is being interviewed by police, who say they've confirmed the shootings were done by one man, but it's believed a second person may have been involved.
ABC reporters at the scene say it's now understood the gunman has escaped.
The coroner has arrived at the scene and he's examining the two bodies in the building.
BOND PLEADS GUILTY AFTER DEAL WITH PROSECUTORS
Jailed former tycoon, Alan Bond, appeared in the Supreme Court in Perth today to admit his part in the nation's biggest case of corporate fraud.

In a deal with the Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions, Bond agreed to plead guilty to two charges of failing to act honestly as a director of a company in return for the dropping of a series of other charges.
The charges relate to the transfer of one-billion dollars from Bell Resources to Bond Corporation in the late 1980s.
Early next year Justice Michael Murray will hear submissions on what sentence Bond should receive: each charge carries a maximum penalty of five year's jail.
In the meantime, Bond has been returned to prison to continue serving his three year jail sentence imposed earlier this year for art fraud offences.
His appeal against that conviction and sentence has been put on hold while these latest charges are dealt with.
EVANS: GROWTH FIGURES REFLECT SLUGGISH ECONOMY
Shadow Treasurer, Gareth Evans, says today's economic growth figures reflect a sluggish economy.
National accounts figures for the September quarter show growth at 3.8 percent, up 0.8 percent.
The Government claims the figures show the economy is growing solidly with a low inflation base and in-line with budget forecasts.
But Mr Evans says the figures are bad news for unemployed people.
He says they show the economy is growing at no more than about two percent, which is only about half the rate required to bring the unemployment rate down.
ACCUSED SHAKEN AND UPSET: WITNESSES
A Wollongong court has heard, that 18 year-old Matthew De Gruchy, who's accused of killing his mother, sister, and brother, was visibly upset when ambulance officers arrived at the murder scene.
Officers Allan Taylor and David Garvey were among the first to attend the Albion Park home in March, were the dead were found.
Officer Taylor told the court that Matthew De Gruchy looked upset and appeared to be crying when they arrived.
Officer Garvey agreed, saying he was emotional and shaking all over.
They took the accused to hospital for counselling and sedation, and Officer Garvey said that on the way, he heard the accused say "what has happened".
ACTU DEFENDS WAGE CLAIM
The ACTU has defended its living wage claim saying it's well within Reserve Bank wages forecasts and won't hinder low inflation.
The claim seeks a minimum wage of 380-dollars a week, and a 20-dollar increase for workers who haven't had a rise through enterprise bargaining.
Union President Jennie George has condemned the Government's offer of an eight-dollar a week wage rise as pathetic.
But she's admitted the ACTU's claim involves a rise of just over two percent, and doesn't ensure a reasonable standard of living for low income families.
An Industrial Relations Commission hearing in Melbourne has heard an official survey shows the average low-income family needs 495-dollars to live comfortably.
PLEBISCITE FOR PEOPLE, NOT CONVENTION: BEAZLEY
Federal Opposition leader Kim Beazley says a plebiscite should be held on the issue of Australia becoming a republic.
Mr Beazley says that would give Australians ownership of the issue, and see a compromise on the Government's plan to conduct a people's convention on the issue next year.
The Opposition says it doesn't agree the convention is the right way to go, but says it wouldn't actively oppose the concept.
Mr Beazley says if a plebiscite showed people are in favour of moving towards a republic, a parliamentary committee would investigate the best option...with a referendum held in 1999.
FRASER "RECOVERING WELL" - MANAGER
Sporting champion Dawn Fraser will remain in hospital over the weekend, but her manager says her heart condition isn't serious and she's recovering well.
The Olympian was admitted to Griffith hospital with chest pains on Saturday, and flown yesterday to St. Vincents hospital in Sydney.
It's the fourth time Ms Fraser has been hospitalised with chest pains since she suffered an angina attack at the Atlanta Olympics.
EUTHANASIA VOTE EXPECTED NEXT WEEK
The House of Representatives is expected to vote on over-riding the Northern Territory's euthanasia laws early next week.
MPs are today continuing to debate the private members bill put forward by Liberal back-bencher Kevin Andrews.
Both major parties are allowing a conscience vote on the issue - so it's not clear what the outcome will be and the Senate's not expected to vote on the bill until next year.
Meanwhile, the son of the first person to die under the Northern Territory's euthansia law, is in a stable condition in Bowral hospital in New South Wales after suffering a heart attack.
Yesterday Mr Dent, a member of the Liberal Party, announced he no longer supported the right-to-die legislation, but denied he was subjected to any political pressure.
SOCCER: LOCAL TALENT FIRST PRIORITY FOR VENABLES
New Socceroo coach, Terry Venables, says he will concentrate on locally based players when he announces a squad for the four nation tournament in January.
Venables says he's trying to arrange further matches in February or March in Europe to look at the overseas based contingent.
He says after a week of looking at videos of players with assistant coach Raul Blanco in London, he's satisfied he has good talent to work with.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
